dpa_name: Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL)
submission_channels: Online complaint wizard
pre_complaint_expectation: Choose the complaint theme, identify yourself, describe the issue, and provide supporting material where relevant.
evidence_or_form_notes: CNIL states that identification, complaint description, and supporting documents where relevant are necessary to handle the file.
follow_up_notes: CNIL routes and investigates complaints; European cooperation can apply for cross-border files.
scope_notes: Good first route for France-based complaints and French-facing controllers; check cross-border lead-authority issues for large platforms.

dpa_name: Die Bundesbeauftragte fuer den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit (BfDI)
submission_channels: BfDI online complaint form plus contact channels
pre_complaint_expectation: Identify the target body first; BfDI covers federal bodies, telecom/post providers, and certain special sectors, while most private-sector cases go to a Land DPA.
evidence_or_form_notes: Use the BfDI contact finder or the Land DPA route if the complaint is against a normal private company or a regional or local public body.
follow_up_notes: The official BfDI complaint page says the authority must inform the complainant about status within three months.
scope_notes: Germany is federated for data protection supervision; scope matching matters before filing.

submission_channels: Online concern form or email to info@dataprotection.ie
pre_complaint_expectation: The DPC expects you to contact the organisation first and use the DPC route if the issue is unresolved or the response is inadequate.
evidence_or_form_notes: The DPC asks for copies of the correspondence exchanged with the controller, including full emails with headers, footers, dates, and times visible.
follow_up_notes: The DPC says you receive an immediate acknowledgement of initial contact and aims to provide a substantive response within 20 working days.
scope_notes: High-value route for Ireland-based complaints and many cross-border tech cases handled from Ireland.

dpa_name: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
submission_channels: Official forms and services pages
pre_complaint_expectation: Use the official complaint model or service route published by the Garante; rights-request disputes should usually be documented before escalation.
evidence_or_form_notes: The forms page includes an information page and complaint model; the Italian route is more form-driven than some peers.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this first pass; verify current handling notes on the forms page before filing.
scope_notes: Central Italian DPA route; useful for rights, complaint, and formal filing workflows.

submission_channels: Online complaint or tip-off form
pre_complaint_expectation: The AP says you must first complain to the organisation itself or make a rights request before filing with the AP.
evidence_or_form_notes: The AP notes that if you file a personal complaint, it discloses your identity to the organisation or person concerned.
follow_up_notes: The AP says you will hear from it within three months; it may resolve the matter simply, investigate extensively, or forward a cross-border case while staying your contact point.
scope_notes: Useful for Netherlands-based complaints and EU-headquartered-in-the-Netherlands cross-border cases.

dpa_name: Agencia Espanola de Proteccion de Datos (AEPD)
submission_channels: Electronic Office complaint forms
pre_complaint_expectation: AEPD expects evidence or indications of infringement and uses different filing paths depending on the complaint type, including rights-not-answered cases.
evidence_or_form_notes: Use the complaint path that matches the issue category; the FAQ points to separate Electronic Office routes for rights requests, advertising, debt files, and other infringements.
follow_up_notes: AEPD says it has up to three months to decide on admission or non-admission; after that point the complaint is deemed admitted if no decision has issued.
scope_notes: Strong route for Spain-based rights and complaint filings, especially where the issue fits a standard AEPD complaint category.

submission_channels: Traditional written complaint, electronic inbox, ePUAP, or biznes.gov.pl
pre_complaint_expectation: Use the official complaint route and channel guidance; electronic filing is channel-specific and form-based.
evidence_or_form_notes: UODO distinguishes between the official electronic inbox routes and fallback email use for people without qualified signature or ePUAP trusted profile.
follow_up_notes: UODO says that after investigating the case, if an infringement is confirmed, the President can order compliance by administrative decision.
scope_notes: Useful first route for Poland-based GDPR complaints; the contact page explains the practical differences between filing channels.

submission_channels: Online complaint form, email to dsb@dsb.gv.at, or postal filing
pre_complaint_expectation: This is a formal legal remedy; identify the opposing party and the allegedly violated right clearly before filing.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority page lists mandatory complaint contents, including the opposing party, address, facts, timing, and copies of prior rights requests where applicable.
follow_up_notes: No short processing-time target was captured in this pass, but the page explains filing deadlines: normally within one year from knowledge and no later than three years after the event.
scope_notes: Useful for Austria-based complaints; cross-border private-sector cases can trigger one-stop-shop cooperation and take longer.

dpa_name: Autorite de protection des donnees / Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit (APD-GBA)
submission_channels: Complaint page during citizen-portal transition; verify current portal status before filing
pre_complaint_expectation: The authority strongly suggests checking whether mediation or an information request is more appropriate before using the complaint route.
evidence_or_form_notes: As of April 24, 2026 the authority states that electronic citizen forms are temporarily unavailable and that a new citizen portal is due to open on May 8, 2026. A rights-based complaint normally requires prior exercise of rights and a one-month wait for the controller's response.
follow_up_notes: The page says identity is in principle disclosed to the opposing party and that the First Line Service may treat a complaint first as mediation where appropriate.
scope_notes: Important route for Belgium-based complaints, but current portal transition means citizens should verify the live filing channel before acting.

submission_channels: MitID-backed complaint form, with fallback contact routes if the form cannot be used
pre_complaint_expectation: Datatilsynet recommends contacting the controller first before filing the complaint.
evidence_or_form_notes: The complaint form helps the complainant provide the information necessary for handling the case; the authority requires at minimum a name and address and does not normally handle anonymous complaints.
follow_up_notes: Datatilsynet states a service goal that 50 percent of complaint cases should finish within two months and 80 percent within six months.
scope_notes: Good first route for Denmark-based complaints, especially where the complainant can use the official form with MitID.

submission_channels: IMY e-service, with email or letter fallback in some cases
pre_complaint_expectation: IMY recommends contacting the organisation first, especially for rights complaints such as access, erasure, or rectification.
evidence_or_form_notes: To count as a complaint, the filing must identify the controller and provide contact details; anonymous filings or complaints about someone else's data are treated as tips instead.
follow_up_notes: IMY says it will always reply if the complaint meets the formal requirements and will send a copy of the inspection decision if an inspection is opened.
scope_notes: Strong route for Sweden-based complaints; the page also notes that the complainant may choose another EEA authority for cross-border cases.

dpa_name: Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman
submission_channels: Email or post to the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman; verify current contact path before filing
pre_complaint_expectation: No direct complaint-form page was located in this pass; this route is based on the authority's official legal-protection and case-processing pages.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority says instituted cases receive a record number, may be anonymous, and may involve cooperation with other EU or EEA supervisory authorities.
follow_up_notes: The authority states that decisions of the Office can be appealed to the competent Administrative Court.
scope_notes: Useful official legal-protection route for Finland, but the practical complaint-entry path should be checked again in a later pass for a more direct filing page.

submission_channels: Official complaint form
pre_complaint_expectation: The CNPD asks data subjects to contact the data controller first to assert their rights before filing a complaint, unless that proves difficult or impossible.
evidence_or_form_notes: The rights page says the CNPD first checks whether the complaint is justified and whether the alleged facts are likely to constitute an infringement.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Strong route for Luxembourg-based complaints; good fit where rights requests have already failed or proved impracticable.

dpa_name: Comissao Nacional de Protecao de Dados (CNPD)
submission_channels: Written online complaint forms by issue type
pre_complaint_expectation: CNPD distinguishes complaint forms by subject matter and expects the complainant to choose the form that matches the issue.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority says the forms are designed to collect the minimum information needed for a preliminary analysis and faster routing; if the issue is really an information request, a different form should be used.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful Portugal route because the CNPD now exposes a citizen-facing complaints section with a general form and topic-specific paths.

submission_channels: Complaint page and issue-specific status tool
pre_complaint_expectation: Use the official complaint page to check that the issue is within UOOU competence; the page explicitly excludes several matters that are not really data-protection supervision cases.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority page explains that some problems belong with labour inspection, police, media operators, or courts rather than the data protection authority.
follow_up_notes: For at least some complaint types the authority offers a status-check tool tied to the submitted complaint.
scope_notes: Useful route for Czechia-based complaints, especially once the issue is confirmed to be a true personal-data processing matter.

dpa_name: Office for Personal Data Protection of the Slovak Republic
submission_channels: Written filing, authorised electronic filing, or personal oral submission into minutes
pre_complaint_expectation: The complaint must be submitted in Slovak; the official English page says an official translation is not required.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority's proceedings page explains that an ordinary unauthorised email must be completed within three working days in writing, with authorised electronic filing, or personally into minutes.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Strong route for Slovakia-based complaints; the channel rules matter because ordinary email alone is not enough.

submission_channels: Personal filing, post, fax, or email to azop@azop.hr
pre_complaint_expectation: Anyone who believes a GDPR right or a right under the Croatian implementation act has been violated may submit a request for determination of a rights violation.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority page says the request must be understandable and complete and lists the main personal data and facts that need to be included.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful Croatia route for rights-based complaints and straightforward supervisory requests.

submission_channels: Complaint link on the inspectorate site, with digitally signed electronic submissions or post
pre_complaint_expectation: The inspectorate routes the data-protection complaint according to its legal nature, so the same filing may be treated as a complaint, challenge, or memorandum depending on content.
evidence_or_form_notes: The site says electronic submissions should be digitally signed and sent to info@aki.ee; paper submissions may be posted to Tatari 39, 10134 Tallinn.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful official route for Estonia, though the live complaint page itself is currently exposed through the Estonian-language contact path.

submission_channels: Complaint service page with official complaint sample
pre_complaint_expectation: The complaint should identify the allegedly unlawful processor, the relationship to that processor, the nature of the processing, and whether the complainant has already contacted the processor.
evidence_or_form_notes: The service page says supporting documents should be attached and links to the official complaint sample.
follow_up_notes: The service page says the Inspectorate shall provide a response no later than three months under GDPR Article 78(2).
scope_notes: Strong route for Latvia-based complaints with a clear official service page and timing signal.

submission_channels: Recommended complaint form plus written submission rules
pre_complaint_expectation: The complaint form expects identification of the respondent, the relationship to that respondent, subject matter, whether the controller was contacted first, and attached evidence.
evidence_or_form_notes: The official English materials say the authority must be addressed in Lithuanian and that non-signed email submissions do not satisfy the normal request rules.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful Lithuania route because the official site exposes the complaint form and evidentiary structure clearly, even though the practical filing route is more formal than some peers.

submission_channels: Registry, post, email, or electronic form
pre_complaint_expectation: Romania expects the complainant first to address the controller for GDPR rights and then complain with evidence if no answer arrives within one month or the answer is unsatisfactory.
evidence_or_form_notes: The procedure page says complaints may be filed in Romanian or English, in writing, by post, email, at the registry, or by using the authority's electronic form.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass, but the page stresses admissibility requirements and the need for evidence and controller identification.
scope_notes: Strong route for Romania-based complaints once the rights-request stage and evidentiary threshold are met.

submission_channels: In person, by post, fax, email with qualified electronic signature, or via the secure electronic service system
pre_complaint_expectation: Complaints and alerts must be translated into Bulgarian.
evidence_or_form_notes: The CPDP page sets out the minimum required contents and says email complaints must be electronic documents signed with a qualified electronic signature; scanned unsigned complaints sent by email are not acted on.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Strong route for Bulgaria-based complaints because the official page is explicit about channels and formal requirements.

submission_channels: Form B complaint route and investigation procedure guidance
pre_complaint_expectation: The authority uses a specific complaint form for breaches of the legislation for the processing of personal data.
evidence_or_form_notes: The investigation procedure document identifies Form B as the complaint route for personal-data processing breaches and lists the Commissioner's office as the filing authority.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful Cyprus route, but this row should be refined later with a cleaner web page if one becomes available.

submission_channels: Online portal with taxisnet credentials, or English-by-email fallback in some cross-border cases
pre_complaint_expectation: For rights complaints under GDPR Articles 15 to 22, the complainant must normally have exercised rights with the controller first and either received no answer within one month or received an unsatisfactory answer.
evidence_or_form_notes: The page says complaints should be filed in the appropriate form with directly linked supporting documents and notes an English-by-email fallback when the complainant cannot use the Greek login route and Greece is the place of the alleged infringement.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Strong route for Greece-based complaints and cross-border cases where Greece is the place of the alleged infringement.

dpa_name: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH)
submission_channels: Authority inquiry or administrative procedure for data protection
pre_complaint_expectation: The NAIH distinguishes between inquiries and administrative procedures for data protection; the complainant route depends on whether the data subject seeks a formal procedure or a lower-formality inquiry.
evidence_or_form_notes: The authority's English material says anonymous notifications may ground an inquiry, while a data subject whose data rights are infringed can submit an application to commence an administrative procedure for data protection.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Useful Hungary route, though it still needs a later pass to locate the clearest citizen-facing filing instructions or forms.

submission_channels: Dedicated online complaint form; electronic complaints should use the online form
pre_complaint_expectation: Malta expects the data subject to engage the controller first in rights-based cases and then complain if there is no response within one month or the reply is unsatisfactory.
evidence_or_form_notes: The IDPC contact page says data protection complaints filed electronically shall only be lodged using its dedicated online form.
follow_up_notes: No short timing statement was captured in this pass.
scope_notes: Strong Malta route because the authority clearly separates the complaint form from general contact and ties it to the data subject rights section.

dpa_name: Information Commissioner of the Republic of Slovenia
submission_channels: Online form, email to gp.ip-rs.si, or ordinary mail
pre_complaint_expectation: Anyone can submit a report if they feel that someone is violating the GDPR or the Slovenian Personal Data Protection Act.
evidence_or_form_notes: The Information Commissioner recommends using the appropriate form and states that the report may be sent by email or ordinary mail; the site also says an online form is available for reporting violations.
follow_up_notes: The authority says it will try to provide an answer in the shortest time possible.
scope_notes: Strong Slovenia route for reports and complaint-style supervisory interventions.
